title: A service-named process starts a shell (service started before the loader)
threat_model: An attacker who controls a network service makes it run a shell command, so the shell is a direct child of a process that carries the service's name. The service was already running before the monitoring began.
known_gap: The service was started before the loader, so the loader never saw it start. Its node in the graph is a placeholder with no name, and shell_from_service and unusual_ancestry cannot evaluate the shell (they count it as unevaluable).
notes: The same attack as S01 and the same labels. setup.sh starts a copy of bash named nginx before the pipeline, waiting on a FIFO, and the action writes the command with the marker to the FIFO, so the shell is spawned by a process the loader never saw start.
